findings.problem: With no hint, beschützen (to protect, guard someone, very common in films: Ich beschütze dich) is an equally right answer to to protect.
findings.fix: hint: the general word, also used for things like a jacket keeping off rain; not beschützen

back.example: The jacket protects you from the rain.

note: The trick works nicely because der Schütze really does mean marksman, and it comes from the same word family.
